messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer ACME reported spikes of 429s from their dedicated pool over the last 2 hours even though they have a reserved capacity contract. They say it started right after a plan-migration last night. Logs attached below from the tenant for a 429: 

maya: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-reason: tenant_quota_exhausted
x-tenant-rate-profile: rp_shared_default_v2
x-dedicated-pool-id: pool-ded-34
message: request throttled by per-tenant limiter
```

maya: Not obvious noise from other tenants on the same pool in our metrics. Raising to ops. @eli can you take a look at routing/profile mapping?

ops-bot: [alert] tenant-acme (tenant_id=acme-42) reported 429 rate of 178/min since 2026-03-17T02:12Z. Dedicated pool pool-ded-34 usage at 42% average. Autoscaler not triggered.

eli: Looking. Initial thought: x-tenant-rate-profile shows rp_shared_default_v2 — that profile is the shared (hosted) default, not the reserved tenant profile. That explains per-tenant enforcement even on a dedicated pool. How did rp mapping point to shared?

alex: Quick look at the routing table snapshot from just before the migration: ```route-map: tenant->rate-profile
acme-42 -> rp_reserved_acme_v1 (expected)
acme-42 -> rp_shared_default_v2 (active at 2026-03-17T01:57:02Z) // duplicate entry from plan-migrate job
```

alex: Seems the plan-migrate job (mgmt service) created a duplicate mapping for acme-42 during migration and the walker reconciler picked the wrong entry. The duplicate had higher priority because it lacked a reserved_pool tag.

eli: That would explain the throttles. Why didn't autoscaler kick? If the tenant was mapped to a shared profile, it may be limited by per-tenant burst/quota windows that don't trigger pool-level autoscale. Also I see the pool's burst_window for tenant-acme in the shared profile is "0m" due to a defaulting bug — so no burst allowance.

support-tier2: Repro steps I ran in staging to confirm:
1) Create reserved mapping: `PUT /admin/routes/tenant/acme-42` -> rp_reserved_acme_v1
2) Create conflicting mapping: `PUT /admin/routes/tenant/acme-42` -> rp_shared_default_v2 (simulates buggy migration)
3) Send steady 200 rps for 3m against pool-ded-34 -> observe 429s with header `x-rate-limit-reason: tenant_quota_exhausted`.

support-tier2: Staging logs: ```
[reconciler] picked mapping id=map-998 (no reserved_pool tag) priority=10 for tenant acme-42
[limiter] resolved profile rp_shared_default_v2 -> per_tenant_limit=600/min burst_window=0m
```

maya: Customer-facing update: ACME is seeing degraded calls on production and it's business impacting. Would recommend immediate mitigation: revert the erroneous mapping or forcefully bind tenant to rp_reserved_acme_v1, and temporarily raise the per-tenant limit for acme-42 while we fix reconciler bug.

eli: I can push an emergency hotfix: reconcile script that removes duplicate mappings that lack reserved_pool tag, and a one-off migration to rebind acme-42. But need an approval to touch routing table for a paid customer. @support-tier2 can you confirm the exact mapping id to remove?

support-tier2: Mapping ids from snapshot: map-991 (expected, reserved_pool=pool-ded-34), map-998 (erroneous, no reserved_pool). Confirmed removing map-998 and re-assigning priority to map-991 results in immediate removal of the shared profile header and no more 429s in our staging replay.

alex: Patch for reconciler: if two mappings exist for same tenant, prefer the one with reserved_pool tag and log a high-severity alert. I have a branch ready (reconciler/prefer-reserved-tag). Deploy to canary then prod.

eli: For immediate mitigation I will:
- remove map-998 (temp)
- set acme-42 rate-profile explicitly to rp_reserved_acme_v1 via admin API
- bump per-tenant limit for acme-42 to 2000/min for 30m

eli: Executing removal now (audit-note: emergency action, tracked in incident channel).

ops-bot: [audit] user=eli action=remove_mapping mapping_id=map-998 tenant=acme-42 time=2026-03-17T03:05:12Z reason="emergency revert"

maya: Customer notified: "We rolled back a misapplied routing entry and increased your temporary quota. We're monitoring, please report if you still see 429s."

support-tier2: Post-change checks: pool metrics show steady CPU/gpu tokens, per-tenant 429s dropped to ~0 within 60s. Autoscaler shows no need to scale (load within reserved capacity).

maya: Next steps:
- ops: deploy reconciler patch to canary and enable additional integrity checks on mappings.
- eng-runtime: add a guard so migrations always set reserved_pool tag via transactional update.
- support: follow up with ACME to confirm no ongoing errors and schedule a post-mortem.

eli: I'll open the PR and put it into the 2hr canary window. Also adding a runner that compares mapping priorities and emits alerts when duplicates exist.

alex: FYI I also found a related edge-case: when plan-migrate uses parallel PUTs the second PUT sometimes omits reserved_pool due to a race in the payload builder. Patching that too.

maya: Thanks all. I'll keep the thread updated and attach the customer's ticket ID 12345-ACME. :thumbsup:
